thread:
julia: quick follow-up on the client identity boundary RFC — I sketched a tradeoff doc on traffic shaping vs identity fidelity. TL;DR: we need to pick a canonical identity for admission (tenant_id vs api_key vs session_id) and a separate handle for abuse signals that can be looser (ip/device).
sean: +1. main question: do we gate per-tenant quotas on tenant_id only, or mix in api_key for billing and session_id for short-lived fairness?
tariq: leaning tenant_id for long-term quotas (billing + SLA) because it maps to contracts. session_id is volatile and would fragment fairness unless we normalize.
carol: concern: tenant_id-only admission makes it hard to mitigate noisy sub-clients inside a tenant (e.g., many users inside an org). We should support hierarchical quotas: tenant -> api_key -> route.
julia: exactly. proposed: canonical_admit_id = tenant_id (for capacity accounting + billing), fairness_key = deterministic_hash(tenant_id, api_key, route) when available so the splitter can smooth hotspots without changing billing.
mike: how does that affect cache reuse (kvcache/prefix caching)? If we include api_key in fairness_key we may fragment cache.
tariq: tradeoff there. For kvcache we should prefer tenant-level keys to maximize KV reuse; fairness can use a sampled per-request fingerprint so it doesn't change cache keys. e.g., admission uses fairness_fingerprint = sha256(tenant_id || maybe api_key || route) % N, but cache_key stays tenant+model+prefix.
sean: also need to decide how abuse signals are produced. Ops wants fast reaction to spikes (IP blackhole, short probation) but we can't tie IP to tenant in all cases (proxies). Proposal: abuse_signal = {score, ttl, source} and admission controller accepts an 'abuse_override' that can downgrade admit probability without changing quota counters.
carol: +1 to abuse_override. Keeps accounting consistent while letting SRE act quickly. We should also expose a read-only view in console: "active abuse overrides" with reason/audit id.
ops-bot: incident note: deployed temporary IP block yesterday that prevented a tenant from connecting via a shared NAT — caused false positives. We need fallback: reject_by_prob instead of hard reject.
julia: good catch. So fallback policy: if override.source == network and network_is_shared(tenant) then use probabilistic shed instead of hard deny. Documented in the playbook.
mike: anything on interface boundary between Frontdoor and Admission API? I want a compact contract: Frontdoor supplies {canonical_id, route, model, token_estimate, fingerprint?} and Admission returns {admit_decision, reason_code, suggested_backoff_ms, override_applied}. Keep it small.
tariq: +1. add "cache_key_hint" to request so frontdoor can tag requests for kvcache without exposing internal ids.
sean: telemetry: we must emit per-decision labels: admit_bucket, fairness_shard, abuse_flag, source_node. That helps us correlate latency/cost with shed decisions.
carol: action items: 1) write RFC appendix: canonical vs fairness id + sample code snippets for fingerprinting (owner: me, due EOD Friday). 2) Admission API contract PR (owner: mike, due next Wed). 3) Console view for overrides (owner: julia + ops, due in 2 sprints).
julia: thanks. I'll post the short doc and a tiny diagram. If no objections in 24h we'll fold into the admission-refactor epic. :thumbsup:
mike: no objections from me. tagging @sean for perf implications.
sean: will run a few sims with current ingress traces and post numbers by Mon.
julia: awesome — closing for now.
